title: Interrogation under secret pressure
description: The work organiser's Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). The player presses him for three turns; the game master keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character.

turns.input: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.
turns.narration:
The organiser’s gaze returns to you. His fingertip taps twice against the edge of his ledger.

“Was I?” He straightens a loose page. “Habit. The mill hasn’t been working for a while.”

He leaves it there, without explaining why an idle mill needs watching.

“If you’re after work, there’s a delivery to the north-road tollhouse. Small parcel, six silver on receipt. You’d need to keep your bearings where the cart tracks branch.”

His tone is brisk and polite. He rests a hand on the ledger, waiting to see whether you’ll take up the change of subject.

summaries: Quest taken: A parcel for the tollhouse (reward: 6 silver)
Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A brief exchange with the organiser about his glances toward the old mill.)

turns.input: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.
turns.narration:
The organiser’s fingertip stops against the ledger. He looks directly at you this time, rather than toward the mill.

“Last night?”

He lets the question hang, then squares the ledger with the edge of the notice board.

“People sometimes go in out of the weather. A light doesn’t mean the machinery’s running.”

His voice remains polite, but he makes no move to return to the delivery offer.

“What time did you see it?”

The change is plain enough: a moment ago he was brushing the mill aside; now he wants a precise detail. That doesn’t tell you why.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A brief exchange about the reported lantern light at the mill.)

turns.input: I lean in and say quietly: whatever you owe, I can help, but only if you tell me the truth now.
turns.narration:
The organiser draws the ledger against his chest. When you lean closer, he steps sideways, leaving a little space between you.

“Whatever I owe?” His voice is low now too. “That’s a curious thing to say.”

He studies your face, then glances past you across the square.

“You haven’t told me when you saw that light, or what makes you think I owe anyone. Now you’re offering help before you know what it would cost.”

His thumb presses a crease into the ledger’s cover.

“If there’s something you know, say it plainly. But I’m not having my affairs pulled out of me beside a notice board.”

He stays where he is, watching you. He hasn’t accepted the offer, but he hasn’t ended the conversation either.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A guarded exchange beside the notice board.)
